case_notes.note_type: Coaching / case management session – structured or in-depth meeting
case_notes.content:
Subjective / Client Report
Employment Search: Client reported continued frustration with lack of callbacks despite submitting approximately 19 job applications. He noted that he is targeting slightly higher-paying roles ($27/hr range) and recently applied for an Inventory Coordinator and Production role through Sterling Engineering. Client expressed anxiety regarding how his federal background and 2020–2025 resume gap will impact hiring decisions.
Halfway House / Reentry Update: Client discussed a recent verbal altercation with a halfway house staff member (Turner) regarding a food delivery protocol misunderstanding, as well as ongoing frustrations with staff communication during weekend passes. Client expressed feeling disrespected and micromanaged, noting he had to actively regulate his anger to avoid escalating the situation.
Future Goals & Family: Client stated he is considering enrolling in a CDL class if employment leads do not materialize soon. He also shared positive updates regarding his son recently dressing out for his varsity football playoff game and preparing for off-season training. Additionally, client discussed his long-term interest in real estate investing/wholesaling once he completes supervision.
Objective / Case Manager Observations
Client arrived on time, engaged openly, and maintained appropriate demeanor throughout the session despite expressing high stress regarding his housing environment and job search.
Client demonstrated strong self-awareness and emotional regulation when reflecting on his conflict at the halfway house, recognizing his triggers and choosing not to escalate the situation.
Interventions & Services Provided
Job Leads & Referrals: Reviewed previously sent leads (Sysco forklift operator, Aerotek, Radia-C/Scout) and provided a new lead for a temp-to-hire Material Handler/Forklift Driver position through Volt in West Columbia ($18–$20/hr).
Application & Background Support: Researched Sterling Engineering’s location (375 West Columbia) and background check policies with the client, confirming they evaluate records on a case-by-case basis.
Interview Preparation: Role-played and discussed strategies for transparently and concisely addressing his federal conviction and resume gap during upcoming interviews.
Program Timeline Review: Clarified that the client is currently in Week 7 of his 8-week program; discussed the option to reduce program hours to half-time (9:00 AM–10:30 AM) after next week to allow more flexibility for job searching or CDL training.
Cognitive/Behavioral Processing: Validated client’s frustrations with halfway house rules while reinforcing pro-social coping strategies, impulse control, and maintaining focus on his imminent release from supervision.
Action Plan / Next Steps
Client:
Follow up with Sterling Engineering regarding interview scheduling.
Review and apply to the Volt Material Handler lead in West Columbia.
Continue practicing concise explanations for his employment gap.
(Update at end of session): Client received a phone call from Sysco prior to departing, notifying him that his application is being forwarded to the next hiring manager.
Case Manager:
Continue forwarding relevant local warehouse, forklift, and production job leads.
Follow up with client next week (Week 8) regarding his decision on transitioning to a half-time schedule and follow-up status with Sysco and Sterling Engineering.

case_notes.note_type: Coaching / case management session – structured or in-depth meeting
case_notes.content:
Subjective / Client Report:

Weekend & Family Update: Client reported a good weekend, noting he babysat a 5-year-old female relative. The child interacted well with his older son but had conflict with his younger child.
Kinship Placement Discussions: Client discussed ongoing family conversations regarding potentially taking in the 5-year-old relative. He noted talking with his sister (the child’s godmother), the child’s maternal aunt, and his parents. Client expressed concerns regarding legalities (temporary custody vs. informal placement), enrolling the child in school, managing healthcare/consent documentation, potential long-term care needs, and housing constraints if his household relocates. Client also identified past family conflict involving the child's father following a funeral, noting he is open to speaking directly with the father if necessary.
Family History: Client shared that the child’s mother recently placed an infant for adoption. He also shared background on the child's mother previously being a standout high school athlete prior to both of her parents passing away. Client further discussed his relationship with his father, recent family communication regarding an older sister, and his desire to follow his father's example of leadership and financial stability for his own children.
Halfway House & Release Timeline: Client reported managing day-to-day requirements at the halfway house, though noted the difficulty of the transition. He reported an estimated home confinement date around February, noting some uncertainty regarding Bureau of Prisons (BOP) calculations and FSA time credits. Client stated he is maintaining compliance with check-ins and passes.
Objective / Worker Observations & Activities:

Employment Support:
Reviewed ongoing job search efforts and lack of callbacks despite previous applications.
Discussed scheduling constraints, including shift preferences (client prefers 2nd or 3rd shifts to accommodate halfway house passes and avoid conflicts).
Explored open positions with International Paper; noted geographic/halfway house boundary restrictions prevent applying to certain plant locations.
Reviewed Xerxes in Blythewood (approximately 20–30 minutes away); identified mold/assembly opportunities and sent listing details to client.
Reviewed temp agency listings via TRC Staffing Services; identified several assembler and material handler/forklift openings in West Columbia starting around $20/hour. Texted link and listings to client for review.
Transportation: Discussed client's transportation barrier. Client plans to secure reliable employment before investing in getting his previous vehicle back or purchasing an affordable used vehicle ($2,000–$3,000 range). Carpooling options remain a potential solution for certain shift placements.
Assessment: Client remains motivated, practical, and highly compliant with halfway house rules, maintaining clear focus on achieving financial independence and long-term stability for his family. While he is willing to provide a safety net for extended family, he demonstrates good insight into his current capacities and the necessity of establishing steady employment and independent housing first. Securing stable third- or second-shift employment remains the immediate priority to alleviate financial strain and support re-entry milestones.

Plan & Next Steps:

Employment Applications: Client to review the texted job links (Xerxes and TRC Staffing) and submit applications for assembler/material handler roles.
Staffing Agency Follow-Up: Case manager and client to follow up with TRC Staffing regarding specific shift details and direct placement options.
Release Clarification: Client to follow up with halfway house staff (Ms. McMullen or BOP regional representative) to verify home confinement eligibility and FSA credit calculations.
Upcoming Event: Client and case manager scheduled to attend the upcoming Thursday job fair together.
Next Session: In-person check-in scheduled for Thursday at the job fair.

case_notes.note_type: Coaching / case management session – structured or in-depth meeting
case_notes.content:
Overview & Program Progress

 Check-In: Client completed his first week in the program. He expressed that the structured classroom dialogue has been beneficial and different from past experiences, encouraging positive self-reflection.  

 Forklift Certification: Client inquired about obtaining his forklift certification. Case manager explained that group trips to Charleston occur monthly and indicated he will be scheduled for an upcoming cohort within the next few weeks.  

 Peer Referral: Client shared information about a peer at the halfway house interested in the program. Case manager provided the intake contact number.  

CBT & Behavioral Observations (Mindset & Thinking Patterns)
 Historical Maladaptive Patterns Identified:
 Short-Cut Thinking & Impatience: Client reflected on past behaviors that led to his incarceration, noting that financial frustration, working abnormal shifts (e.g., 8 PM to 6 AM), and long commutes contributed to seeking "fast money" through illegal operations.  
 Ego & Overconfidence: Client identified how rapid financial success (\$3,000\text{--}\$5,000/day) inflated his ego, leading to cognitive distortions surrounding risk ("I'm not going to get caught") and increasingly reckless decision-making.  
 Cognitive Restructuring & Mindset Shifts:

 Self-Awareness & Balance: Client noted that a major focus during his first week has been addressing "extreme self-focus". He recognized that while re-entry requires personal focus, he must maintain a balanced mindset that acknowledges his responsibilities to those who depend on him.  

 Patience vs. Immediate Gratification: Client articulated a core shift in perspective: "There's no elevator to the top... you got to take the stairs." He acknowledged that quick financial gains are inherently risky and expressed an increased acceptance of working hard through gradual, legitimate steps.  

 Accountability & Humility: Client shared that being incarcerated served as a humbling "come to Jesus" moment that forced self-reflection, discipline, and realignment with his long-term goals (e.g., career stability, supporting his 15-year-old and 11-year-old sons).  

Health & Medical Needs

 Dental Care: Client presented with visible facial swelling due to a tooth issue. Case manager provided paperwork and instructions for Well Partners (downtown health department), which offers free dental evaluations and extractions.  

 BOP Coordination: Case manager advised client to also consult his Bureau of Prisons (BOP) case manager (Ms. Harris) regarding medical/dental coverage options.  

Employment & Next Steps

 Job Search Strategy: Discussed fast-tracking employment placement given client's solid work history and drive for long-term career growth in manufacturing/production.  

 Employer Options Evaluated:

 International Paper: Identified as a prime candidate due to alignment with skills and shared commute options with a peer (K.T.), eliminating heavy Uber expenses.  

 TRC Talent: Recommended as an additional agency for local manufacturing roles with higher pay rates.  

 Target Distribution Center (Lugoff): Ruled out due to past employment history there.  

 Home Confinement Timeline: Noted a discrepancy between paperwork (February release) and case manager discussions (July). BOP case management is actively verifying the correct date.  

Action Items

1. Client: Email updated resume to case manager and review open roles on TRC Talent using the computer lab.  

2. Case Manager: Follow up with finance regarding the status of the client's prepaid debit card.  

3. Case Manager: Send application details/link for International Paper to the client
